NATO strengthens eastern flank amid rising tensions

Allied defence ministers agreed on Tuesday to deploy additional troops and air defence systems to member states bordering Russia and Belarus, citing a deteriorating security environment in the region.

The decision follows months of discussions about the readiness of forward-deployed forces and the speed with which reinforcements could be moved across the continent in the event of a crisis.

Officials stressed that the measures were defensive in nature and proportionate to the threats identified by the alliance's military planners during the latest review of regional plans.

Several governments also announced national programmes to modernise civil protection, including shelters, early warning systems and public information campaigns aimed at households.
